## A generated module, not an abstract character match

Under a nonzero Q-compatible pure-V radical, use the canonical homotopy h and only the fixed negative linear space W. Define

    F2=im h,     F3=X_W(F2),     F4=T_(Sym²W)(F2).

These actual subspaces form a fixed-variable negative submodule, and Q(F2)⊂F4. The exact first two characters and dimensions are

    F2=P+D,  dim F2=9;
    F3=W′+2T,  dim F3=14,  T=Sym⁵W.

The first-arrow cokernel on P(W) is O(5)⊕P O(1). This describes the actual restricted first arrows; it does not identify the whole three-space module with a previous radical image or split its second arrows. In particular the middle dimension differs from the older radical-image modules.

## Why the middle dimension is forced

The genuine first-pencil bundle B has an equivariant bundle splitting (P+D)O(2)⊕A O(6)⊕O(18), used only for cohomology, not as a horizontal module decomposition. The evaluation exact sequence computes the actual joint first-multiplication kernel as

    ker(W⊗N2→N3)=W+2S+3T.

The embedded pure-V image I=(D,T,P) has first-multiplication kernel S. Passing to U=N/I by the snake lemma gives ker(W⊗U2→U3)=W+S+3T, containing no W′.

The canonical P-isotypical summand P_h of im h embeds in U2. Since W⊗P_h=W′+T, a nonzero restricted kernel would have to contain all of T, leaving image dimension at most two. But the established first-arrow injection off the reduced twelve-point divisor restricts injectively to this four-dimensional P_h. Thus W⊗P_h→U3 is injective. Consequently

    F3=I3⊕X_W P_h=T⊕(W⊗P).

This actual direct sum yields the displayed cokernel via binary multiplication and the free P evaluation system. It uses the everywhere-off-divisor theorem, not a chosen direction or a character-only inference.

## Endpoint alternatives retain their relations

Commutativity gives Y_W F3=F4; the sandwich identity gives F4⊂ker h. Also F4 contains I4=P and Q(F2)=I4. There is an actual surjection

    Sym²W⊗P_h→F4/I4→0.

Since Sym²W⊗P=V+P+D is multiplicity-free, the necessary endpoint characters are P+ε_V V+ε_P P+ε_D D, with each ε equal to zero or one. The possible dimensions are therefore

    {4,7,8,9,11,12,13,16}.

This is a necessary list, not eight realized cases or a selected endpoint. In particular the 28-dimensional ker h is only a container, not the generated target. The kernel of the displayed surjection retains the actual quadratic relations. Its lift to I4⊕(Sym²W⊗P_h) can have a graph component into I4 only through the P constituent; neither that scalar nor channel occurrence is determined. No pending target refinement is included.

## Conditional smallest-endpoint consequence

If F4=I4, Q:P_h→I4 is an isomorphism. Write s for its inverse and Z for the universal negative quadratic formal perturbation. Then (Q+Z)s=1+Zs has a formal inverse. For every d∈D,

    d(z)=d−s(1+Zs)⁻¹(Q+Z)d

is a formal kernel lift with d(0)=d. Hence all five original D classes lift simultaneously and all their later Bockstein obstructions vanish. The original 37-minors vanish as polynomials on Q+Sym²W; the generic rank on that affine family is exactly 36, using the invariant rank 33 and generic rank-three second symbol for the lower bound.

This alternative implies zero canonical two-channel lift via the original-fourth comparison. The converse is not proved. Neither this endpoint nor an actual coefficient is selected, and no source pair is removed. The claim is restricted to the specified affine family, not all ambient quadrics or a formal splitting of the full graded module.

This construction starts from im h=P+D in degree two. It is separate from the collaborator's [canonical W→A→S→D string](89-canonical-negative-string-source-report.md), which begins in degree one without selecting the pure-V branch.
